Location: Earman River at US 1, North Palm Beach (side channel off Lake Worth / Atlantic ICW)
Item: Earman River channel closed to boats at the US 1 bridge through spring 2027
Details: The Earman River channel under the US 1 bridge in North Palm Beach is closed to boaters while the bridge is replaced; southbound road traffic has moved onto the new span. Why it matters: boats kept up the Earman River (C-17 canal) can't get out to Lake Worth and the ICW this way until spring 2027. The main ICW channel itself isn't affected.
When: Through spring 2027 (exact reopening date not given)
Notes: What to do: if your boat is on the Earman River, plan on it staying put or check with FDOT District 4 about any passage windows. Source is a local news roundup (Oct 18); I couldn't find the Coast Guard notice itself, so confirm in the current Southeast District LNM. Map point is the US 1 crossing, approximate.

Location: Long Beach Yacht Club, Long Beach MS – racing on Mississippi Sound south of the LBYC harbor
Item: Melges 15 Youth Team Challenge at Long Beach Yacht Club
Details: Youth team racing in Melges 15 dinghies: teams of at least five sailors aged 18 and under rotate through the boats, seven races scheduled on Mississippi Sound just off the harbor, with electronic (Vakaros RaceSense) starts. Why it matters: short windward-leeward races close to shore make this an easy one to watch from the Long Beach harbor or the beach – a good look at the next generation of Gulf Coast sailors.
When: Sat Nov 7 (first warning 12:30pm) – Sun Nov 8 2026 (no starts after 2pm)
Notes: What to do: watch from the Long Beach harbor area Saturday afternoon or Sunday late morning; if you're anchoring or passing by on the Sound, give the racecourse south of the harbor a wide berth. Contact: regatta chair Krista Clark (email on the NOR). Same weekend as the Jimmy Buffett Race in Jacksonville, Sailing Sisters at DIYC and the start of the A-Class Cat Worlds in Tampa. Map point is the LBYC harbor, approximate.

Location: Halifax Sailing Association, Daytona Beach (Halifax River)
Item: 5th Pink Ribbon Regatta – racing for breast-cancer awareness
Details: Halifax Sailing Association's Windward Women host a one-day dinghy and multihull regatta (Sunfish, Laser, RS Aero, Capri 14, 420, FJ, multihulls, plus a youth Opti division) that raises money for Halifax Health's cancer center and a New Smyrna Beach breast-care boutique. Why it matters: a friendly, cause-driven small-boat regatta on the Halifax River along the Atlantic ICW – easy to watch, and day-of entries are taken.
When: Sat Nov 14 2026; first warning noon, last warning 3pm, awards and taco dinner 5pm
Notes: What to do: register on Regatta Network or on site that morning (add $25 late fee); PRO Chris Sinnett (860) 389-7924. ICW traffic past Daytona should expect small boats racing near the channel Saturday afternoon. Embry-Riddle's Turkey Trot Regatta is the next day (Sun Nov 15) at the same club. Same weekend as the Jubilee Regatta in Pensacola and the Penfield Flying Scot Regatta in Sarasota. NOR gives only the organizer's mailing address, so the map point is Daytona Beach on the Halifax River, approximate.

Location: Coconut Grove Sailing Club, 2990 S Bayshore Dr, Miami – racing on Biscayne Bay ~1.5 nm SE of the club
Item: Finn Class North American Championship in Coconut Grove
Details: The Finn – the heavy singlehanded Olympic dinghy – brings its North Americans to Biscayne Bay, up to eight races over three days, with trophies down to a 'Top Legend' for sailors over 70. Why it matters: big-muscle singlehanded racing about 1.5 nm off Coconut Grove; worth a look from the Dinner Key area, and cruisers crossing the bay should expect a racecourse there Fri–Sun afternoons.
When: Thu Nov 19 (check-in) – Sun Nov 22 2026; racing Fri–Sun from noon
Notes: What to do: if you're crossing Biscayne Bay near Coconut Grove those afternoons, keep clear of the course; race committee works VHF 16, 68, 69, 71 and 73. CGSC office (305) 444-4571. Same weekend as the J/70 Mixed Plus Nationals in St. Pete and the Egmont Key Race from DIYC (Nov 21–22).

Location: St. Petersburg Yacht Club, St. Petersburg (Tampa Bay)
Item: J/70 Mixed Plus Nationals at St. Petersburg Yacht Club
Details: St. Petersburg Yacht Club lists the J/70 Mixed Plus Nationals – a national championship for mixed-gender J/70 crews – on its 2026–27 regatta schedule. Why it matters: a fleet of J/70 one-designs racing off downtown St. Pete; good watching from the waterfront parks, and boats heading in and out of the downtown marinas should expect a busy bay.
Notes: What to do: check spyc.org for the notice of race and racing area before you go. Dates come from the club's 'preliminary' schedule (updated Oct 3) – I couldn't find the notice of race yet, so confirm. Same weekend as the Egmont Key Race from Davis Island YC (Nov 21–22) and the Finn North Americans in Miami.
